sources.citation: Theil, Rolf. n.d. romani – språk. Store norske leksikon (snl.no).
sources.note: Encyclopaedia article by the leading specialist; no sound-system, stress or tone information. Lists Sundt 1850, Iversen 1944, Ribsskog 1945, Karlsen 1993/1995, Theil et al. 2014 (Vandriane rakkrar) as literature.

sources.citation: Theil, Rolf. 2014. Romani, språket til taterane. Språknytt 42(4): 23-25. Oslo: Språkrådet.
sources.note: Open (CC BY-NC-ND) at nb.no, item a921df51fa..., pages 23-25 fetched sources via IIIF and scanned (tesseract eng model). Popular-science article on the first book in Norwegian Romani; the only phonological remark is 'Norsk romani er også sterkt påverka av det norsk-svenske lydsystemet' (p. 24: Norwegian Romani is also strongly influenced by the Norwegian-Swedish sound system). Nothing on stress or tonal accent; no hit for 'trykk'/'tonelag' on pp. 23-25.

sources.citation: Sundt, Eilert. 1850. Beretning om Fante- eller Landstrygerfolket i Norge: Bidrag til Kundskab om de laveste Samfundsforholde. Christiania.
sources.note: Public-domain older primary (Romani/Rodi wordlist). The archive.org text layer is Fraktur scanned garbage and only the eng tesseract model is installed, so it was not examined for a stress remark; nb.no fragment hits 'Tonen' (p. 325), 'Tonefald' (p. 100), 'Tryk' (p. 69) are unverified. Not treated as a stress source.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page trav1236 (Traveller Norwegian); en.wikipedia 'Scandoromani' (redirect from Traveller Norwegian); no.wikipedia 'Norsk romani'
sources.note: Glottolog: alt. names Rodi / Norwegian Traveller, ISO rmg, classified as a Speech Register; descriptive ref Iversen 1944. Wikipedia articles give morphosyntax only; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Iversen, Ragnvald. 1944. Secret languages in Norway. Part I: The Romany language in Norway. Oslo: Jacob Dybwad (Skrifter utg. av Det Norske Videnskaps-Akademi i Oslo II, 1944 no. 3). 275 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only full description of Norwegian Romani; full-text index shows 'Accent (Stress)' p. 232, 'Penultimate Stress' p. 233, 'Musical Accent' pp. 234-237 and stress-notation remarks p. 23 — the deciding statement is there. Digitised at Nasjonalbiblioteket (item 107c49cedbcad4be7dfcebd164b36389, URN:NBN:no-nb_digibok_2017041248038) but viewable only from a Norwegian IP / Feide login; otherwise print (OCLC 3536966; Stanford and other US copies).

sources.citation: Wiedner, Jakob Anton Paul. 2017. (De)mystifying Norwegian Romani – the discursive construction of a minority language. PhD dissertation, University of Oslo. 292 pp.

sources.note: Most recent academic monograph on Norwegian Romani (Norsk romani-prosjektet, UiO/ILN); likely contains a structural sketch with prosody remarks and a full review of Iversen. No open file in NVA/DUO.

sources.citation: Carling, Gerd, Lenny Lindell & Gilbert Ambrazaitis. 2014. Scandoromani: Remnants of a Mixed Language. Leiden: Brill (Brill's Studies in Language, Cognition and Culture 7). Ch. 2, §2.5 Word-level prosody.

sources.access_detail: Harvard print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID WID-LC P130.52.S34 C37 2014
sources.note: Most authoritative modern phonological description of Scandoromani (Swedish side, with F0 measurements); states initial-stress default with penultimate/final exceptions and Accent I/II; the introduction compares Norwegian Romani and cites Iversen — the closest modern statement for trav1236 pending Iversen.
